8.0.0.en: The elders of Israel: they are the king's counselors, who help him in ruling in the cases of the people.

8.0.1.en: The heads of the tribes, the chief of the fathers: their number is 12, one for each tribe.

8.0.2.en: The city of David, Zion: it was first a fortress of the Jebusites, and afterward David took it and built in it a palace and a new city called by his name (1 Chr 11:4-8). The word Zion means "fortress," and it is one of the hills on which Jerusalem stands. David had brought the ark to it, and then Solomon moved the ark to the Temple that he built on Mount Moriah; that is, Zion is not Mount Moriah. Later the word Zion came to include the Temple as well, and the name Zion is often applied to the whole of Jerusalem.

8.0.3.en: The last place to which the ark had come was Zion, in a special tent that David pitched for it, which was different from the original tabernacle that Moses had made, which was set up at Gibeon and contained all the furnishings of the tabernacle. Since Solomon's Temple was built on Mount Moriah, it was natural that the ark be moved from Zion to the Temple to be placed in the Holy of Holies. It was fitting that the move take place in a festive manner, in a procession in which the elders of Israel and the heads of the tribes walked, whom King Solomon had invited to take part, for it was a celebration proclaiming God's dwelling in the midst of all the people and the dedication of the Temple. The word "bring up" does not mean moving the ark from a low place to a high place, but to the house of God, the greatest place in the world.

8.1.0.en: The month Ethanim: it is the seventh month in the Hebrew calendar of the religious year and the first month of the civil year, and it corresponds to September and October; the feasts of Atonement, Trumpets and Tabernacles fell in this month.

8.1.1.en: All the men of Israel answered the king's call, and all the religious and civil leaders and the representatives of the people took part in the celebration for moving the ark, which the king himself presided over, and this took place in the month of Ethanim.

8.1.2.en: The Temple had been completed in the month of Bul, that is, the eighth month, and Solomon waited eleven months, in which he finished the furnishings and the vessels inside the Temple and arranged everything connected with the celebration of the dedication of the Temple. He chose the seventh month of the following year because it is full of feasts, as we have mentioned, and the people gather in it from all the land as the Law prescribes. Thus, after about 480 years in which worship continued in the tabernacle of meeting, it now moved to a built and permanent Temple, Solomon's Temple.

8.2.0.en: The tabernacle: what is meant is the tabernacle that Moses made.

8.2.1.en: The priests carried the ark on their shoulders, as the Law prescribes. Carrying the ark was the work of the Levites, but because of the greatness of this celebration the priests themselves carried the ark. The tabernacle of meeting was at that time in another place outside Jerusalem, namely "Gibeon" (1 Chr 16:39), so all the furnishings and vessels that were in the tabernacle, and the tabernacle as well, were moved and kept in the chambers attached to the house of the Lord, because they had been sanctified by God's presence in them during the prayers, so they were a blessing that had to be preserved. Thus we understand that the ark was in one place, Jerusalem, while the tabernacle and its vessels were in Gibeon in the days of David, and all this was moved to the Temple.

8.2.2.en: The tabernacle of meeting signifies the body of Christ in which He lived on earth, and the entry of the tabernacle into the house of God that Solomon built signifies the entry of Christ with His luminous body into heaven after His ascension.

8.3.0.en: In their procession before the ark, the king and the people offered sacrifices in numbers too many to be counted or numbered, to express their joy and their thanks to the Lord for His work with them and for His allowing a permanent Temple to be built in which He would dwell in their midst.

8.4.0.en: The priests brought the ark into the Holy of Holies and placed it in the place appointed for it under the wings of the cherubim made of olive wood overlaid with gold (ch. 6:27).

8.5.0.en: The wings of the cherubim overshadowed the ark, and the staves appointed for carrying the ark were in their places in the rings on the sides of the ark, until the ark was brought into its place.

8.6.0.en: After the priests brought in the ark with the two staves by which they carried it, they placed it under the wings of the cherubim standing in the Holy of Holies. Then they drew the two staves outward toward the door of the Holy of Holies, but did not remove them from the rings. They would shine when the high priest entered the Holy of Holies, in the divine light (the Shekinah) that shone at his entering; and so the shining of the ends of the staves could be seen, so that he would not come near the ark.

8.6.1.en: When the two staves were drawn out, the priests who were standing in the Holy Place at that time saw the ends of the two staves, and then they closed the door of the Holy of Holies, so that no one saw them any longer except the high priest when he entered once every year. The two staves were no longer used to carry the ark, because it had come to rest in the Holy of Holies and there was no need to move it, as used to happen in the past in the tabernacle of meeting. The tabernacle signifies the Church sojourning in the wilderness of the world, while the Temple signifies the heavenly Jerusalem, where the Church rests with Christ forever.

8.6.2.en: The presence of the two staves in their rings on the ark, although it had come to rest in the Holy of Holies, reminds us believers of the necessity of constant vigilance in our spiritual striving, which will not end until we enjoy entering eternal life. We must also always realize that we are strangers on this earth until we return to our heavenly home.

8.7.0.en: There was nothing inside the ark except the two tablets of the Law; as for the pot of manna and Aaron's rod, which the Apostle Paul mentioned in (Heb 9:4), they were placed in a special chest beside the ark in the sanctuary. The pot of manna and Aaron's rod used to be set in the tabernacle of meeting before the ark of the covenant (Num 17:10), and then placed in it when they set out on a journey; but in the Temple, after they had settled, they were placed before the ark in a special chest.

8.8.0.en: When the priests came out of the Holy Place after placing the ark in its place, a thick cloud appeared and filled the Temple, as a sign of God's satisfaction with what King Solomon and his people had done. The density of the cloud was extremely noticeable, so that the priests were not able to begin the service. This is the same thing that happened at the dedication of the tabernacle of meeting, when Moses was not able to enter (Ex 40:34-35). God did not appear in His glory until after the priests had gone out, because they could not bear to see the glory of God.

8.8.1.en: Note: the priests placed the ark of the covenant in the Holy of Holies and then went out before the beginning of the service, and after that no one was permitted to enter the Holy of Holies except the high priest, and only once a year. The glory of God appeared in the form of a cloud for the following reasons:

8.8.2.en: 1- The cloud is high in the sky, and God is exalted above our thoughts and our works.

8.8.3.en: 2- The cloud is pure water that evaporated and rose to the sky, and God is pure, indeed perfectly pure.

8.8.4.en: 3- The cloud is white in color, and God is all radiance and majesty.

8.8.5.en: 4- The cloud hides what is behind it, and God, no one knows the depths of His essence, because He is unlimited, and it is not possible to know all His thoughts and plans.

8.8.6.en: The cloud proclaims the presence of God in many places, as in the Transfiguration of Christ on the mountain. But the mystery of the appearing of the cloud proclaims the glory of God and His esteem for this Temple, and His appreciation of the labor of Solomon and all his people in building it with such magnificence; and the true mystery of greatness is the indwelling of God, not the splendor of the building.

8.8.7.en: The glory of the Lord, when it filled the house, signifies the body of Christ in the fullness of time, and also the dwelling of His Holy Spirit in the heart of every believer in the New Testament, in addition to His dwelling in His Church and His Holy Sacraments. (2) The fulfillment of God's promise (vv. 12-21)

8.8.8.en: 12- Then spake Solomon, The LORD said that he would dwell in the thick darkness. 13- I have surely built thee an house to dwell in, a settled place for thee to abide in for ever. 14- And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the congregation of Israel: (and all the congregation of Israel stood;) 15- And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, which spake with his mouth unto David my father, and hath with his hand fulfilled it, saying, 16- Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build an house, that my name might be therein; but I chose David to be over my people Israel. 17- And it was in the heart of David my father to build an house for the name of the LORD God of Israel. 18- And the LORD said unto David my father, Whereas it was in thine heart to build an house unto my name, thou didst well that it was in thine heart. 19- Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name. 20- And the LORD hath performed his word that he spake, and I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and have built an house for the name of the LORD God of Israel.

8.8.9.en: 21- And I have set there a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant of the LORD, which he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.

8.9.0.en: Solomon stood to encourage the people, since their hearts were filled with awe when the glory of the Lord filled the house with the cloud, and he made his people understand that the cloud is a proclamation of God's presence in the midst of His people and His dwelling in His house. God had appeared in the cloud before that, in the days of Moses the prophet, and it seems that this expression, that is, God's dwelling in the cloud, was known among the Jews, since they used to see it settle upon the tabernacle of meeting; but Solomon confirms it here, when he saw the cloud covering the house of the Lord at its dedication.

8.10.0.en: Solomon began a sermon that is in essence a hymn of thanksgiving to God for what He permitted by fulfilling the desire of David his father, enabling his son Solomon to build a house in which the Lord would dwell forever.

8.11.0.en: Solomon's face had been toward the Holy of Holies when the ark was brought into it, so he turned around to face his people standing before him and to bless them with the blessing with which the high priest blesses the people, as Moses the prophet blessed them (Ex 39:43) and as David did when he brought up the ark of the Lord to the city of David (2 Sam 6:18). The words of the blessing that Solomon said are not recorded, and perhaps they resemble what the high priest says (Num 6:22-27). The people needed to be reassured by this blessing in the face of the awe of God's indwelling and the fear of Him.

8.12.0.en: Solomon refers to the divine promise to David to build the house (2 Sam 7), praising the Lord, who promised first with His mouth, and then fulfilled with His hand what He had previously promised.

8.13.0.en: Solomon said, speaking of the mouth of the Lord, that the Lord had not specified for the people, since He brought them out of Egypt, any particular city among the cities of the tribes of Israel in which to build a house in the name of the Lord, but chose David as king over His people. Solomon had heard these words from his father, to whom Nathan the prophet had made them known (2 Sam 7). And it was David who thought of building the house, as Nathan the prophet told (2 Sam 7). God was dwelling in the midst of His people, in the tabernacle of meeting, which moved from place to place among the tribes, until God permitted a permanent house to be built for Him.

8.13.1.en: When God saw David's desire to build a house for Him, and then Solomon's carrying it out, He rejoiced, and came to dwell in the Temple and blessed it. And when God sees your longing and your striving toward Him through prayer and reading, He rejoices and blesses your life with many blessings beyond what you hope for.

8.14.0.en: God rejoiced at David's desire to build a house for God, but because David was occupied with many wars, to enlarge the kingdom and establish it, it was not fitting for him to build this great house, so He postponed this work to the days of his son Solomon, in whose reign there was stability and prosperity.

8.15.0.en: Solomon adds, saying: the Lord fulfilled what He promised, so I, his son, took over the throne, and I built the house in the name of the Lord, and I prepared a place for the ark, which holds the covenant of the Lord that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of Egypt, that is, the two tablets of the Law on which the commandments are written.

8.15.1.en: We notice in Solomon's words that he did not refer to the grandeur of the buildings of the house of God, or to the gold in it, but focused on two matters, namely:

8.15.2.en: 1- God's promise to build a house for Him by the hand of the son of David.

8.15.3.en: 2- The presence of the ark of God's covenant in the Temple.

8.15.4.en: That is, the greatness of the Temple rests on God's promise and His presence through the ark, and this is the secret of the Temple's strength, which is the image of heaven on earth.

8.15.5.en: (3) Praise of God and the covenant with Him (vv. 22-27)

8.15.6.en: 22- And Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread forth his hands toward heaven:

8.15.7.en: 23- And he said, LORD God of Israel, there is no God like thee, in heaven above, or on earth beneath, who keepest covenant and mercy with thy servants that walk before thee with all their heart: 24- Who hast kept with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him: thou spakest also with thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it with thine hand, as it is this day. 25- Therefore now, LORD God of Israel, keep with thy servant David my father that thou promisedst him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel; so that thy children take heed to their way, that they walk before me as thou hast walked before me. 26- And now, O God of Israel, let thy word, I pray thee, be verified, which thou spakest unto thy servant David my father. 27- But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?

8.16.0.en: The altar of the Lord: what is meant is the bronze altar, before which a platform was set up for Solomon, and all the people stood behind him.

8.16.1.en: Solomon turned his face toward the altar of the Lord, leading all the people in their supplication to God, and lifted his hands toward heaven to praise the Lord. This shows Solomon's godliness and his understanding of the holy worship offered to God. And spreading out the hands means:

8.16.3.en: 2- Presenting requests and needs to God, who is able to answer them.

8.16.4.en: 3- Showing humility and reverence in supplicating to God.

8.16.5.en: 4- Proclaiming faith in God's dwelling in heaven, that is, His being exalted above the thoughts of men.

8.16.6.en: 5- Praising God and glorifying Him for His mercies and gifts.

8.16.7.en: The believers still lift up their hands to God in their prayers, whether the common prayers in the Church or the private prayers in their homes.

8.16.8.en: And Solomon, in this intercessory prayer for his people, is a type of Christ the Intercessor for His people (Jn 17). Solomon stood before the altar because his prayer rests on the sacrifice, which signifies the sacrifice of Christ; for by Christ our Redeemer we have access and boldness before the Father.

8.17.0.en: Through his praise, Solomon acknowledges that God has no likeness and no equal, neither in heaven nor on earth; He is the maker of mercy by fulfilling the divine promises, and He is a faithful God who keeps the covenant and kindness for those who love Him and keep His commandments, who walk in His ways uprightly. He is steadfast in keeping His promises despite the weakness of men and their failure to keep their promises toward Him, and then His mercy covers and completes every weakness in men; by His keeping of His promises and by His mercy, He receives His children despite their weakness.

8.18.0.en: God is true in His promises, and He had promised David to permit a house to be built for Him, and now by the power of God the divine promise has been fulfilled, and the house has been built by the hand of David's son, that is, Solomon the prophet.

8.19.0.en: Now Solomon asks the Lord to continue the kingship over the children of Israel for the house of David, as He promised him, saying that there would always be one of his offspring sitting on the throne of the kingdom, on condition that they keep the commandments and are faithful and upright (2 Sam 7:4-17). And God fulfilled His promise to the offspring of David: after the kingdom was divided, He left two tribes for the offspring of David to reign over, and this is the kingdom of Judah; then the greatest fulfillment of this promise came when Christ came from the offspring of David to reign over the hearts of those who believe in Him forever.

8.20.0.en: With his spiritual wisdom, Solomon realized that God, who fills every place, had condescended and was pleased to dwell in a specific place in the midst of His people.

8.20.1.en: May you glorify God in your prayers and praise Him, so that you may feel His greatness, and so stand in reverence before Him and receive His blessings, and ask of Him with confidence everything you want, for He is the Great One, who is able to do all things.

8.20.3.en: 28- Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer, which thy servant prayeth before thee to day: 29- That thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which thou hast said, My name shall be there: that thou mayest hearken unto the prayer which thy servant shall make toward this place. 30- And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, when they shall pray toward this place: and hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place: and when thou hearest, forgive. 31- If any man trespass against his neighbour, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to swear, and the oath come before thine altar in this house: 32- Then hear thou in heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness. 33- When thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee, and shall turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray, and make supplication unto thee in this house: 34- Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land which thou gavest unto their fathers. 35- When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toward this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, when thou afflictest them: 36- Then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, that thou teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and give rain upon thy land, which thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.

8.20.4.en: 37- If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, blasting, mildew, locust, or if there be caterpillar; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there be; 38- What prayer and supplication soever be made by any man, or by all thy people Israel, which shall know every man the plague of his own heart, and spread forth his hands toward this house:

8.20.5.en: 39- Then hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and forgive, and do, and give to every man according to his ways, whose heart thou knowest; (for thou, even thou only, knowest the hearts of all the children of men;) 40- That they may fear thee all the days that they live in the land which thou gavest unto our fathers. 41- Moreover concerning a stranger, that is not of thy people Israel, but cometh out of a far country for thy name's sake; 42- (For they shall hear of thy great name, and of thy strong hand, and of thy stretched out arm;) when he shall come and pray toward this house; 43- Hear thou in heaven thy dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for: that all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee, as do thy people Israel; and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by thy name. 44- If thy people go out to battle against their enemy, whithersoever thou shalt send them, and shall pray unto the LORD toward the city which thou hast chosen, and toward the house that I have built for thy name: 45- Then hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause. 46- If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near; 47- Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness; 48- And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen, and the house which I have built for thy name: 49- Then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy dwelling place, and maintain their cause, 50- And forgive thy people that have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions wherein they have transgressed against thee, and give them compassion before them who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them: 51- For they be thy people, and thine inheritance, which thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron:

8.20.6.en: 52- That thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them in all that they call for unto thee. 53- For thou didst separate them from among all the people of the earth, to be thine inheritance, as thou spakest by the hand of Moses thy servant, when thou broughtest our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord GOD.

8.21.0.en: Solomon asks the Lord to answer his supplications and prayers that he lifts up to the Lord on this day, and this shows the extent of Solomon's humility and reverence before God, and his sense of the greatness of His presence and also of his own intense need, so he cried out from the depth of his heart, asking for His help.

8.22.0.en: In this place: he means before the house of God.

8.22.1.en: Solomon asked God for His constant care and concern for His Temple and for all the petitions offered in it by Solomon and all the people of God, because the name of God has been called upon this place, and God in His love hears from heaven and forgives His people who cry out to Him that He may have mercy on them.

8.23.0.en: Laid an oath upon him: the person who suffered harm asked the person suspected to swear, in order to confirm his words.

8.23.1.en: If harm befalls a person, and he suspects another of being the cause of the harm that befell him, he brings him to the house of the Lord and has the suspected one swear, and let the Lord be the judge between them: if he swears falsely, the Lord condemns him, and if truly, the Lord justifies him. That is, Solomon asks God to be a judge for His people, so that He blesses the innocent and punishes the guilty, against whom no tangible evidence of guilt has appeared, for God is the searcher of hearts and minds, and thus all injustice is removed and God carries out His justice, punishing the wrongdoer and justifying the innocent.

8.24.0.en: God promised His people that He would keep them if they kept His commandments (Lev 26:1-13), but if they broke and transgressed them, they would be exposed to the attacks of their enemies and be defeated before them (Lev 26:14-39), and after their defeat, if they felt their sins and offered repentance before God toward His holy Temple, Solomon pleads with God to forgive them and bring them back by His power to their land from which the enemies had driven them out, and this is what happened in the captivity.

8.24.1.en: So that you may enjoy God's blessings that He has given you, may you keep His commandments and thank Him at all times, and not despise His long-suffering by persisting in committing sin, lest you lose these blessings.

8.25.0.en: If You withhold from Your people the rain that waters the crops because they sinned against You, and then they realized their error and acknowledged their iniquity and turned from their evil ways because they knew that You were disciplining them for their disobedience, then accept their repentance and answer their supplications and forgive them, and allow the sky to rain and water the land that You gave to Your people to dwell in. This actually happened in the days of Elijah the prophet, when the people left God and were immersed in the worship of Baal, but when they repented, God sent down rain after three years and six months.

8.26.0.en: Blasting: a hot wind that dries up plants and kills them.

8.26.1.en: Mildew: a plague that strikes crops and destroys them.

8.26.2.en: Caterpillar: locusts in the early stages of their growth, which multiply by the millions and are voracious, for it is the most dangerous stage of the growth of locusts.

8.26.3.en: If a famine occurs, or some pestilence spreads, or a scorching wind blows and strikes the crops, or locusts and plagues attack it, or if enemies besiege the cities of Your people, or if a disaster befalls Your people, then when any individual of all Your people prays or supplicates, aware of the transgression he has committed, and spreads out his hands toward this Temple, then answer from heaven, the place of Your dwelling, and pardon, and repay each one according to his ways; for You alone know what goes on in the mind of every man and You know the secrets of hearts, so You forgive the repentant who supplicate You and punish the wicked who persist in their sins.

8.27.0.en: When Your people see Your authority, O God, and Your forgiveness of the repentant and Your repayment of the wicked, they fear You and keep Your commandments.

8.28.0.en: Solomon gives an opportunity to the foreigners, that is, non-Jews, to enjoy praying before the house of God, so he asks Him to answer their petition if they come to Him because they heard of His power, and when He answers them they believe in Him and in His Temple, because of His superiority over their idols, and so they become proclaimers of God's power among the nations. Moses had permitted foreigners who love the people of God to dwell beside them and offer sacrifices to God (Num 15:14). These verses show God's love for the Jews and the Gentiles, which was completed in the fullness of time when Christ died for the salvation of all mankind.

8.29.0.en: If Your people go out to meet an enemy in any place You send them to, that is, a war by the command of the Lord and not from personal motives, and they pray to You, turning their faces toward the city You have chosen and the Temple You have built for Your name, then answer from heaven their prayers and their supplications, and give them victory over their enemies. Whenever they sought God before the war and He sent them to fight the enemies, they were victorious, but when they neglected to seek God they were defeated.

8.30.0.en: Maintain their cause: and rescue them and bring them back to their land.

8.30.1.en: If Your people sin and You permit, O God, their enemies to carry them captive to their own land, and Your people pray toward Your Temple and ask for Your help, then rescue them from the hands of their enemies and bring them back to their land. This actually happened in the Babylonian captivity, and God brought them back by the hand of Cyrus the Persian king (Ezra 7:12, 13).

8.31.0.en: From the midst of the furnace of iron: from the midst of a furnace for smelting iron, and it means hardships and torments.

8.31.1.en: If You permit, O God, Your people to remain for a period in captivity and they supplicate toward Your Temple, then forgive them and make those who carried them captive treat them gently, and shepherd them with Your mercy; for they are Your people whom You rescued from the slavery of Egypt and its torments.

8.32.0.en: May You always be attentive to my supplications to You and likewise the supplications of Your people, and may You answer all their petitions and their cries to You, for You chose them as Your children from among all the peoples, as You said by the tongue of Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt (Deut 4:20). We notice that Solomon focused on the petitions and needs of his people and not on his own petitions and needs, for he represents the faithful servant who cares for those he serves before himself.

8.32.1.en: And we see that Solomon in his prayer relies on God's Law that Moses received, for he holds fast to what the fathers lived by and what God taught them.

8.32.2.en: And the Book of Chronicles (2 Chr 7:1-3) tells us of God's pleasure with this prayer, for fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house, so that the priests could not enter, and all bowed down before the great God who loves His people.

8.32.3.en: God is compassionate: whatever your sins may be, and even if you have been exposed to many problems because of them, He is ready to forgive you and remove all afflictions from you, indeed He honors you and glorifies you because you are His child.

8.32.5.en: 54- And it was so, that when Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication unto the LORD, he arose from before the altar of the LORD, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to heaven. 55- And he stood, and blessed all the congregation of Israel with a loud voice, saying, 56- Blessed be the LORD, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.

8.32.6.en: 57- The LORD our God be with us, as he was with our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us: 58- That he may incline our hearts unto him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers. 59- And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the LORD, be nigh unto the LORD our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel at all times, as the matter shall require: 60- That all the people of the earth may know that the LORD is God, and that there is none else.

8.32.7.en: 61- Let your heart therefore be perfect with the LORD our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.

8.33.0.en: Solomon prayed before the altar of the Lord, bowing on his knees, spreading his hands toward heaven, and then turned toward the people to bless them with a loud voice, and this closing blessing is a summary of Solomon's long prayer before it.

8.34.0.en: Blessed be the LORD: that is, He is worthy of glory and exaltation from His people.

8.34.1.en: Solomon prayed to God and glorified Him, because He gave His people a land to dwell in and find rest from those who troubled them, for He brought them out of the land of Egypt and kept them in the wilderness of Sinai and brought them into the land of Canaan and kept them in the days of the judges and raised up for them a good king, David, and after him his son Solomon, and thus He fulfilled all His good promises that He spoke by the tongue of His servant Moses.

8.35.0.en: Solomon asked God to remain with him and his people as He was with the fathers from the days of Abraham, and not be angry with them or withdraw from them, and to help them, so that their hearts might cling to Him, and they might live by His commandments and worship Him faithfully as the fathers lived with Him.

8.36.0.en: Solomon also pleaded with God to accept his prayers and the prayers of all his people, which they lift up to Him every day, by day and by night, and to care for them and supply all their needs and order all their affairs, and when the nations see what the Lord has done with them, they will acknowledge that the Lord, the God of Israel, is God and there is no other god besides Him.

8.37.0.en: Here Solomon addresses the people, asking of them complete devotion to the Lord and sincere loyalty to Him by walking according to His statutes and obeying His commandments, as they did today, that is, the day of the dedication of the Temple, when they were in spiritual zeal and readiness to obey the commandments of God.

8.37.1.en: May you be steadfast in your relationship with God; when you promise Him that you will live with Him and commit to a specific striving, take care to follow up on these promises so that they do not grow lukewarm and weak. Be careful to renew your promises every day before God, and so enjoy fellowship with Him and rejoice in His care for you.

8.37.3.en: 62- And the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the LORD. 63- And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto the LORD, two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD. 64- The same day did the king hallow the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD: for there he offered burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings: because the brasen altar that was before the LORD was too little to receive the burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings. 65- And at that time Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days, even fourteen days. 66- On the eighth day he sent the people away: and they blessed the king, and went unto their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the LORD had done for David his servant, and for Israel his people.

8.38.0.en: After Solomon's prayer, he offered with his people many sacrifices to God, most of them perhaps peace offerings, which signify thanks to God for what He had done with them, in permitting a house to be built for Him in their midst. And perhaps they offered some sin offerings, that God might forgive them their sins; and likewise some burnt offerings, which signify their readiness to consecrate their hearts to God.

8.39.0.en: The peace offerings that were sacrificed during the period of the celebrations were enormous in number: 22 thousand oxen and 120 thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the people dedicated the house of the Lord.

8.39.1.en: Dedication means consecrating the holy place and beginning to use it and to enjoy worship in it. We notice that the dedication is carried out by prayer and the offering of sacrifices, and this signifies that the consecration of holy places is carried out by the sacrifice of Christ the Savior and by prayer to Him, for without shedding of blood there is no remission (Heb 9:22). The many sacrifices proclaim:

8.39.2.en: 1- The great love of Solomon and his people for God.

8.39.3.en: 2- Their sense of God's greatness and His condescension in having a permanent dwelling in their midst.

8.39.4.en: 3- The wealth of Solomon and his people.

8.39.5.en: 4- Their deep thanks to God for His good pleasure to dwell in a permanent Temple in their midst.

8.39.6.en: 5- Their making a covenant with God by eating of the sacrifices, that they might live for Him.

8.39.7.en: 6- Their acknowledgment of their weakness and sins and their need of God's mercy.

8.39.8.en: These sacrifices were probably not offered in one day but throughout the fourteen days in which the celebrations of the dedication of the Temple continued (v. 65). Most of these sacrifices were probably from Solomon's own money, and the rest from the offerings of the people and their leaders.

8.39.9.en: As for the peace offerings, a part of them was offered to God, the second part was taken by the priests, and the third part that remained was eaten by those who offered the sacrifices, with care to include the Levites, the poor and everyone in need in eating of these sacrifices (Lev 7:11); that is, they offered sacrifices to God, and He gave them of them, and they ate from the hand of God and rejoiced. This shows that the days of the dedication of the Temple were days of very great joy and gladness for all the people.

8.39.10.en: The offering of the sacrifices was accompanied by the sounding of trumpets, the playing of instruments of song and continuous praise of God, most likely by chanting the psalms that glorify God (2 Chr 7:6). And when the Scripture says that Solomon sacrificed these huge numbers, it is implicitly understood that he did not sacrifice them himself, because he is not a priest. The number of the priests was very large, about three thousand, and the Levites who assisted them numbered about 40 thousand. And these sacrifices were carried out, as we said, over a period of 14 days, and therefore it was possible to offer these huge numbers.

8.40.0.en: Solomon made a large bronze altar on which to offer the fat of the sacrifices as the Law prescribes, but no altar, however large, could hold the huge numbers that were offered at the dedication of the Temple. Therefore Solomon was compelled to consecrate a large area at the entrance of the house of the Lord, around the bronze altar, for offering the sacrifices on it, and perhaps he set up temporary altars for this occasion and put on them some of the holy fire that was on the bronze altar (Ex 40). The animal sacrifices, as well as the offerings of flour and other grain offerings, were offered on these altars.

8.41.0.en: Hamath: a Syrian city at a distance of 200 km north of Damascus.

8.41.1.en: The river of Egypt: or the brook of Egypt in some translations, it is the Wadi el-Arish, the last southern boundary of the tribe of Judah, and it is a seasonal stream that fills with water in winter and dries up in summer, and it marks the border between Egypt and the land of the children of Israel.

8.41.2.en: The people of God gathered from the farthest part of the land in the north, that is, from the entrance of Hamath, to its farthest part in the south, which is the river of Egypt; all of them came to Jerusalem to rejoice at the dedication of the Temple, and kept a feast for seven days for this purpose, and this was in the seventh month, before the feast of Tabernacles, which begins on the fifteenth day of it. So after the seven days in which they celebrated the dedication, they continued for another seven days to celebrate the feast of Tabernacles, in which the Law requires all the males of the children of Israel to come to Jerusalem to stand before the house of God. It was a good choice on Solomon's part to choose the occasion of the feast of Tabernacles, in which the people gather from every place, and to place the dedication of the Temple in the seven days before it (Lev 23).

8.42.0.en: The eighth day of the feast of Tabernacles, which is the twenty-first day of the seventh month, is a day of solemn rest, as the Law prescribes, and no work is done in it except prayer and worship (Lev 23:33-36). So after the end of this day Solomon blessed the people, after they had enjoyed the worship of God, and the people responded to him and blessed him; that is, they prayed for blessing for him on account of his care in building the house of the Lord. And here we see the great love between the king and his people and their being bound together in the love of God and the worship of Him, so God covered them with His care and blessing. Then they departed rejoicing and returned to their homes glorifying God.

8.42.1.en: How beautiful it is for you to offer prayers for those around you and encourage them with kind words, for this rejoices the heart of God and rejoices others, and then your own heart rejoices too, especially since others will often pray for you and ask blessing for you, so you live as though you were in heaven.

8.42.2.en: God's appearance to Solomon, his constructions and his trade
